title: Trend line splits the range by day, week or month correctly
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  • {Location-A} has invoices on most days of the last twelve months, so Revenue has a value in every period.
  • Day {Day-A} (for example a Sunday this month) has no clocked time at {Location-A}, while the day before and the day after it do.
  • Day {Day-B} (for example a Saturday) has clocked time at {Location-A}, and the day after it, {Day-C}, has none.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 31 days" and click Apply.
  3. Hover along the Revenue trend line, or count its points, and write down how many points there are and the date each shows.
  4. Click the Revenue pill again, pick a start day and an end day so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 32 days" and click Apply, and do the same.
  5. Do the same with a range of 182 days, then with a range of 183 days.
  6. Set a 31-day range again, hover one point and write down its date and value.
  7. Click Reports in the top bar, click Sales, set the Date control to that single day and read the Totals row Subtotal.
  8. Go back to the Dashboard and set the Technician Utilization tile to a custom range from the day before {Day-A} to the day after {Day-A}.
  9. Look at the Technician Utilization trend line around {Day-A}.
  10. Set the Technician Utilization tile to a custom range from {Day-B} to {Day-C} and look at where the trend line would be.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 3 and 4: 31 days: one point per day (31 points). 32 days: one point per week.
  • Step 5: 182 days: one point per week. 183 days: one point per month.
  • Steps 6 and 7: The hovered day's value equals the Sales report's Totals row Subtotal for that day.
  • Step 9: {Day-A} leaves a gap in the line: the line is not joined across it and does not drop to zero.
  • Step 10: With only one day that has a value, no line is drawn. In its place the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder: a light grey dashed outline with rounded corners, no fill and a grey line-chart icon in the middle, the same height as a trend line. The headline still shows its figure.
  • Steps 3 to 7: If the trend line shows no dates or values when you hover it, count the points instead (zoom the browser in if needed) and write "values not checked by hand" in the result comment for steps 6 and 7.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles), with SV-9579 (Story 7) and SV-9575 (Story 3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S4-R11, S4-R12, S4-R15, S4-R16, S4-R18 and S3-R1 (unchanged since version 42) and S7-R2a (added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 (15:06 UTC) by Chris Ward; the spec's change log (version 46) lists it under 2026-10-14); read 14 Oct 2026. The 731-day and 732-day ranges were removed because a tile's calendar now allows at most 366 days (S7-R2a, Chris Ward's answer 3 of 14 Oct 2026). Design canvas board 03_Range_After (calendar, "Range: N days" readout, Apply) and row 15 (empty-chart placeholder, approved 7 Oct 2026). Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-754bd3a on 10/13/2026).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S4-R12: “A tile shows the empty-chart placeholder in place of its sparkline when fewer than two points in the selected range have a value.”
  • S4-R15: “The placeholder is an outline drawn as a light grey dashed line, with rounded corners and no fill. The tile's background shows through it.”
  • S4-R16: “A line-chart icon, in grey, sits at the center of the placeholder.”
  • S4-R18: “The placeholder changes nothing else on the tile. The headline and the supporting line show their usual values.”
  • S7-R2a: “The control is the same date picker the reports use. Besides the nine presets it offers a calendar for choosing a custom range of up to 366 days, the same limit the reports apply, and a Today button inside the calendar. Today is part of the calendar, not a tenth preset. A custom range is not remembered between visits (S7-R8), and the report opened from the tile shows it as "Custom" (S10-E1).”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-754bd3a on 10/13/2026.
